title: Forge 13: LayerNorm, GELU and the pre-LN transformer block

wrong.post_ln_block.py: post-LN layout: normalises AFTER each residual add (out = LN(x + sublayer(x))), so the residual stream is renormalised at every layer and no longer a clean identity highway
wrong.no_attention_residual.py: forgets the skip connection around attention: x1 = Attn(LN1(x)); the input is thrown away and gradients must squeeze through every layer
wrong.no_ffn_residual.py: forgets the skip connection around the FFN: out = FFN(LN2(x1))
wrong.backward_drops_attention_skip.py: forward is right but backward omits the residual term for attention (returns only the LN1 -> attention path), so dx loses the identity gradient
wrong.backward_drops_ffn_skip.py: forward is right but backward omits the residual term for the FFN (dx1 = LN2/FFN path only)
wrong.shared_layernorm.py: ln2 is the same object as ln1: the second call overwrites the cached statistics of the first, so the backward pass uses the wrong xhat and the two norms cannot learn separate scales
wrong.block_not_causal.py: ignores the causal flag and always runs unmasked attention, so every token reads the future
wrong.block_mutates_input.py: adds the sublayer outputs into x in place (x += ...), silently corrupting the caller's array
wrong.layernorm_over_tokens.py: normalises over the time axis (axis=-2) instead of the feature axis: each feature is standardised across tokens, so a token's output depends on every other token (including future ones)
wrong.layernorm_no_eps.py: eps is dropped from the variance, so a constant token divides 0 by 0 and returns NaN
wrong.layernorm_unbiased_variance.py: uses the unbiased variance (ddof=1); the pinned definition is the biased one, so every output is slightly off
wrong.layernorm_backward_no_mean_terms.py: backward is inv_std * dxhat only: it forgets that the mean and variance also depend on x, so dx is wrong and does not sum to zero over features
wrong.layernorm_dgamma_missing_xhat.py: dgamma sums dout instead of dout * xhat (it equals dbeta)
wrong.gelu_is_relu.py: uses ReLU max(0, x) in place of GELU, so small negative inputs are clipped to zero
wrong.gelu_sigmoid_approximation.py: uses the other well-known approximation x * sigmoid(1.702 x): a legitimate GELU variant, but not the tanh form the spec pins, so values differ by ~1e-2 (the backward matches its own forward, so only the value tests catch it)
wrong.gelu_backward_no_product_rule.py: backward is 0.5 (1 + tanh(.)) only: differentiates the gate but forgets that x multiplies it (drops the 0.5 x tanh' term)
wrong.gelu_backward_missing_cubic_term.py: chain rule through the inner polynomial forgets the 3 * 0.044715 x^2 term, so the derivative is close for small x and wrong for large |x|
wrong.gelu_backward_uses_output.py: treats its x argument as if it were the gelu OUTPUT; the feed-forward caches the activation instead of the pre-activation
wrong.ffn_linear_only.py: forgets the activation: the FFN is two stacked linear maps (W1 W2) and cannot add any nonlinearity
wrong.ffn_bias_grad_not_summed.py: db1 sums over the batch only (axis=0), leaving a (T, d_ff) array instead of a (d_ff,) bias gradient
wrong.ffn_accumulating_grads.py: weight gradients accumulate (+=) across backward calls instead of being set
wrong.ffn_wrong_init_scale.py: W2 is scaled by 1/sqrt(d_model) instead of 1/sqrt(d_ff), so the output variance grows with the expansion factor
wrong.params_forget_biases_and_norms.py: counts only the weight matrices (4 d^2 + 2 d d_ff), forgetting the FFN biases and both LayerNorms
wrong.params_assume_4x_ffn.py: ignores d_ff and hard-codes the textbook expansion d_ff = 4 d
wrong.flops_forget_quadratic_term.py: omits the two T x T attention matmuls, so the cost looks linear in context length
wrong.flops_count_macs.py: counts one operation per multiply-add instead of two, so every FLOP figure is half of the pinned convention
wrong.flops_ffn_single_matmul.py: counts only one FFN matmul (forgets the down-projection)

hints: GELU first. The tanh form is 0.5 x (1 + tanh(c (x + 0.044715 x^3))) with c = sqrt(2/pi). For the backward, let t be the tanh and differentiate the product: gelu'(x) = 0.5 (1 + t) + 0.5 x (1 - t^2) c (1 + 3 * 0.044715 x^2). Check it with finite differences before moving on.

LayerNorm is the one you wrote in Forge 8 with a leading-axes twist: statistics over the last axis only, so each token is normalised on its own. Backward: dx = inv_std / d * (d dxhat - sum(dxhat) - xhat * sum(dxhat * xhat)) with sums over the feature axis; dgamma and dbeta sum over every leading axis.

FeedForward is two matmuls and one GELU. Cache x, h = x W1 + b1 and a = gelu(h). In backward use the pre-activation h in gelu_backward, not the activation a. Biases sum over batch and time: dout.sum(axis=(0, 1)).

The block is x1 = x + attn(ln1(x)); out = x1 + ff(ln2(x1)). The residual add is a fork in the graph, so backward ADDS the two paths: dx1 = dout + ln2_path(dout), then dx = dx1 + ln1_path(dx1). Forget either '+ dout' and gradients have to fight through every layer, which is exactly what residuals exist to avoid.

Counting: attention 4 d^2, FFN 2 d d_ff + d_ff + d, two LayerNorms 4 d. FLOPs: a multiply-add is 2 FLOPs, projections 8 T d^2, the two attention matmuls 4 T^2 d, the FFN 4 T d d_ff. The T^2 term is why long contexts get expensive.
